title: The bus pilot
text: The city transport council met last Thursday and approved a three-month trial of a new bus route between the college and the industrial park. The service will start on the first Monday of next month. Buses will leave the college gate every twenty minutes from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m., and again from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m. They will not run on this route in the middle of the day, and they will not run on Sundays. The fare will match the fare on the existing city service, so students can keep using their current travel cards. Officers said the route was requested after a survey of 600 students and park workers. Many reported that the present bus is crowded between 8 a.m. and 9 a.m., and that the walk from the nearest stop takes about twenty-five minutes. The new buses will stop at the library, the hostel gate, and the park's main entrance. They will not stop at the market. The council has not promised to keep the route after the trial. When the three months end, it will look at only two figures: how many people ride each day, and whether the journey is shorter than the present one. If the buses are less than half full, or if the journey is not faster, the route will be withdrawn. A notice of that decision will be posted on the council website within two weeks of the review. Until then, passengers should not assume that the timetable will stay in place.

title: Remote Fridays
text: From the first Friday of next month, people on the customer-support team may work from home, but only on Fridays and only when their tasks do not require the office phone system. The arrangement is a trial, and it will run for eight weeks. Staff who join it must be online from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. and must set their status in the team chat at the start of the day and again after lunch. Calls that need the office line will stay with colleagues who are in the building. The manager, Ms. Iyer, explained the rule at Monday's meeting. She said the trial was suggested after several people asked for one quieter day to clear written complaints. It is not a general work-from-home policy, and it does not apply to the sales team or to new joiners who are still in their first month. Anyone who misses a customer call, or who is offline for more than fifteen minutes without notice, will be asked to spend the remaining Fridays of the trial in the office. At the end of the eight weeks, Ms. Iyer will compare two things with the previous two months: the number of complaints closed, and the number of calls missed. If both figures are no worse, she will ask the director to extend the trial to the end of the year. If missed calls rise, Friday work from home will stop, even for people who personally had a clean record. Staff who want to take part must tell their team leader by this Wednesday.

title: The library hour
text: The college library will keep later hours on weeknights during the examination period, which begins on 2 November and ends on 20 November. From Monday to Friday in those weeks, the building will close at 10 p.m. instead of the usual 8 p.m. Saturday and Sunday hours will not change, and the library will still close at 5 p.m. on both weekend days. The extra hours apply only to the main reading room and the quiet room. The computer lab on the first floor will close at 8 p.m. as usual, because there are not enough staff to supervise it. title: Supplier change
text: Northwind Foods has written to every restaurant on its city list about a change in deliveries. From 1 October, rice, oil, and packaged spices will come from Harbour Supply instead of the depot Northwind has used for six years. The letter says the change follows a run of late shipments in August, when eleven of forty scheduled deliveries arrived more than a day late. Harbour Supply has promised a morning drop on Tuesdays and Fridays, and an extra Saturday drop in the two weeks before festival dates. Prices of rice and oil will stay at the current rate until 31 December. After that, they may be revised, but Northwind must give restaurants fifteen days' notice before any increase. The spice list will be shorter. Two imported blends that sold poorly will be dropped, while the local blends will remain. Restaurants that want a copy of the new list can download it from the customer page or collect a printed copy from the depot office. Emergency orders are still possible, but the rule is stricter than before. A kitchen that calls before noon can receive the goods the same afternoon if the item is in stock. A call after noon will be treated as an order for the next working day, even if the restaurant says the need is urgent. Northwind will not accept emergency requests by text message. The letter asks managers to name one staff member who may place orders, because Harbour Supply will refuse calls from unknown numbers. Restaurants that do not send that name by 20 September may miss the first Tuesday delivery.

title: Lab rules
text: The science department has changed the rules for booking the chemistry laboratory, and the new rules apply from this Monday. Before a student can reserve a bench, they must finish a short safety quiz on the department website. The quiz has fifteen questions, it may be attempted twice, and a score of at least 80 percent is required. A student who fails both attempts must attend a twenty-minute briefing with a lab assistant before a third attempt is unlocked. The booking page will not open until the pass mark is recorded. Inside the lab, bags must be left on the shelves outside the door. Coats may be hung there as well, but notebooks and glasses cases needed for the practical may be taken in. Any spill, even a small one, must be reported to the assistant at once. Students must not wipe a spill themselves. The department introduced that rule after an incident last semester, when a student tried to clean a bench alone and spread the solution onto a notebook and the floor. The practical timetable itself is unchanged. Sessions still begin at 2 p.m. and end at 4:30 p.m., and groups remain limited to twelve students. What has changed is the penalty for breaking a rule. A student who brings a bag inside, or who fails to report a spill, will lose booking rights for two weeks. Repeat problems will be referred to the head of department. Mr. Rao, who wrote the notice, said the quiz is not meant to replace supervision. An assistant will still be present for the whole session, and students should ask before they use any bottle that is not on their instruction sheet.

title: The internship notice
text: A design studio in Bengaluru has published a notice offering six paid internships, running from 1 June to 31 July. The roles sit with the packaging team, not with the photography unit. Applicants must send a portfolio of three original samples by 15 April, together with a one-page note explaining the brief for each sample. Work copied from a class handout will not be considered. title: Canteen feedback
text: After reading a survey completed by 400 students, the college canteen committee has agreed a set of changes for this term. Two new vegetarian meals will be added at lunch, and the fried snacks that drew the largest number of complaints will be removed from the counter. title: Night shift notice
